thought: Fire's caught proper now, and there's a roof half over my head. First day nearly done and I'm still breathing — that'll do for a start.
diary: First proper day ashore, and I'm writing this by firelight with bracken up to my knees. Got the frame of a lean-to up and a ring of stones round the fire, and tonight, God willing, I won't freeze for it. Cut my hand on something in the wreckage this morning — nothing that won't mend. Tired in a way I don't think sleep alone will fix, but the fire's caught and holding, and that's the whole of my luck today and I'll take it. Tomorrow: the roof, before the weather remembers where it left off.

thought: A fishing boat went by out past the reef tonight, lit up and none the wiser I was here. Didn't wave, didn't shout — too far, too dark. Banked the fire and lay down hungry, thinking on it.
diary: A boat passed this evening, out beyond the reef — the first sign of another living soul since I came ashore. I watched its lights a good while before they went. Didn't call out; it would never have carried, and I hadn't the strength to make a fool of myself for nothing. Belly's empty and won't let me forget it, but the fire's banked and should hold till morning. Next time a boat comes by, I want smoke enough to be seen, not just watched for.

thought: Woke dry under a proper roof for the first time — bed of pine boughs, no ground-chill in my bones. Dragging poles now for a signal tripod. That boat won't slip past me twice.
diary: Slept the whole night under a finished roof and didn't once wake shivering — small thing to be proud of, but I'll take my pride where I find it out here. The dog was at the treeline again this morning, close enough to see her properly this time: thin but not starving, watching me the way I watch the tide. Didn't push it. Today I want poles for a signal tripod, dry wood packed in the middle, so if another boat comes by there's more than moonlight to see me by. Belly's still asking questions I can't fully answer yet, but one thing at a time.

thought: Signal tripod's stood and packed with dry wood — one good thing done. Now it's withies and a funnel mouth for the fish trap, so I'm not living meal to meal on whatever the shore gives up.
